newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * Parliament's senior bodies discussed calling an extraordinary session between July 1-10 to ratify the Romanian-Ukrainian political treaty and pass vital legislation, including a health insurance bill and amendments to the education law and the law on judicial institutions.
* Romania's foreign ministry praised the outcome of a European Union summit in Amsterdam, saying it consolidated the Union's committment to enlargement.

A ministry statement expressed Romania's hopes that enlaXrgement negotiations will start at the same time for all candidates and pledged to continue the country's efforts to comply with EU membership requirements.
* Tension remains high among striking Jiu Valley miners who have rejected the government's offers.
Miners' leaders ruled out a march on the capital or roadblocks among possible new forms of protest.
* Miners from neighbouring areas on Wednesday joined the protest by Jiu Valley miners.
* Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is expected to meet U.S. Vice President Albert Gore, to deliver an by Romanian President Emil Constantinescu in response to a letter from President Bill Clinton.
* Romania will continue to lobby for admission to NATO and will not change its foreign policy priorities, Foreign Minister Adrian Severin told a news conference.
* Severin will visit Britain on June 25 as part of Romanian efforts to win support for quick NATO admission. Severin is expected to meet Foreign Secretary Robin Cook.

* MPs of the ruling coalition partner Democratic Party told a news conference that the coalition had set the principles to modify a land restitution law. It would enable Romanians returning to their homeland to seek the return of their land and allow farming experts or people affected by job cuts to ask for land.
